top.line: The padel shop's path to market: sell one and fulfil it, sell time and trust, and hold no stock until orders force it.
top.para: An early shop is easily made too big. What matters is whether you can make a sale and fulfil it. You sell time, knowledge and trust: an offer takes the problem off the buyer's list whatever the date. Be personal and best effort, start with customers who trust you, promise late and deliver early, sell a few products you vouch for, and avoid stock: the numbers show why. Host on a service that allows a shop.

in-short.line: Sell and fulfil, sell time, be personal, start at home, promise late, few products, no stock, learn.
in-short.para: Keep the site simple, on a host that allows a shop.

sell-one.line: Can you make a sale, and can you fulfil it? It does not have to be efficient; it has to work.
sell-one.para: Paul Graham: solve it manually as long as you can, then automate the bottlenecks.

selling.line: The sleeve stayed on the to-do list for days; an offer at any date would have ended it.
selling.para: Two or three days is not long; the problem using attention is what costs.

personal.line: EverythingPadel, founded by Ewan Ramsden, started from a small shed; a person, not a brand.
personal.para: A personal shop gets a margin of error; the reply to every email is remembered, not verified.

start-here.line: Your first market is the customers who already trust you.
start-here.para: If the coach cannot sell the sleeve he recommended, the trust is there and not working.

promise.line: Say five days and deliver in two; people are upset by broken expectations, not by waiting.
promise.para: Oliver's 1980 model: satisfaction depends on expectation and its disconfirmation; no study tests early delivery directly.

products.line: A few products you use and vouch for, and experiments around them.
products.para: Every product that does not sell is feedback, and every sale shows where people hesitate.

no-stock.line: Buying per order never goes into debt; fifty in stock is €851 down after ten sales.
no-stock.para: Stock pulls ahead only after 38 sales in the illustration, ties up cash, can be damaged and sets a next-day expectation.

university.line: The first three to six months teach shipping, service, fulfilment and returns.
university.para: Scale when fulfilment takes an hour or two a day; Photobox began as a website, an order system and a big printer.

hosting.line: GitHub's terms rule out e-commerce on Pages, and Vercel's free plan is non-commercial.
hosting.para: Netlify's free plan allows commercial projects; Cloudflare Pages has no rule against a shop. This corrects the earlier mock-up's setup.

setup.line: A repository an agent maintains, a CRM in an encrypted vault, email drafted by agents and sent by the person.
setup.para: A dedicated Workspace and Claude account make it a company run by one person.

limits.line: Stock numbers illustrative; two remembered stories unconfirmed; hosting terms change.
limits.para: Cloudflare's position rests on the absence of a rule.

sources.line: EverythingPadel, Photobox and Moonpig sources, Paul Graham, Oliver 1980, Queensland Government, hosting terms.
